sourceBindings.text: Organic matter supports several soil functions. In loss on ignition (LOI), a qualified trainer shows how a dry sample is weighed, heated under a laboratory method, cooled and reweighed. You will explain and calculate the recorded mass loss, then decide what the result does and does not prove.
Explain the order and purpose of the empty-crucible mass, oven-dry sample mass, method-controlled ignition, controlled cooling and final mass without operating the furnace.
Calculate a training LOI percentage from stated masses, using the initial oven-dry soil mass—not soil plus crucible—as the denominator, and report the unit and method.
Explain why LOI is a method-dependent mass-loss estimate, not a universal exact organic-matter value, and why the classroom 3–6% range cannot be imposed on every soil.

sourceBindings.text: A practice record gives C=30.00 g, D=35.00 g and I=34.75 g. A learner divides 0.25 g by 35.00 g.
Subtract C from D to find the initial oven-dry soil mass: 5.00 g.
Subtract I from D to find the loss: 0.25 g.
Divide 0.25 by 5.00, then multiply by 100: 5.0% LOI. State that the masses were invented for practice.
The vessel is excluded from the denominator.

sourceBindings.text: A student wants to take a crucible straight from a hot furnace and weigh it before the trainer has completed the laboratory cooling step.
Stop; a hot vessel is a burn hazard and may not give a stable result.
Only the trained operator follows the site's approved furnace, protection, cooling and weighing procedure.
The learner can record the demonstrated sequence and discuss why the cooling stage matters without touching the apparatus.
Knowing the method is not permission to operate the furnace.

sourceBindings.text: A report shows 2.5% organic matter and a learner insists the classroom table classifies it as deficient.
The example table says Low below 2% and Optimum 3–6%; 2.5% lies in its unclassified gap.
Ask for the laboratory method and regional/soil-specific interpretation, including depth, texture and climate.
Do not prescribe compost at a guessed rate from this number alone.
Unclassified by this table does not mean healthy, unhealthy or zero need.

sourceBindings.text: A trainer reports 5% mass loss under a named method. Someone writes 'exactly 5% organic matter' on the crop plan.
The instrument observed a mass difference, not the composition of each lost component.
Check whether the method and soil composition allow nonorganic mass loss or residual moisture to affect the figure.
Report 5% LOI with its method and seek a calibrated interpretation before calling it exact organic matter.
The measurement and its biological interpretation are different claims.

sourceBindings.text: soil organic matter
Organic materials and their decomposed products in soil, relevant to structure, water and nutrient cycling.
loss on ignition (LOI)
Percent mass lost from an oven-dry sample after heating under a stated laboratory method.
crucible
A heat-resistant laboratory vessel; its own mass is excluded from the dry-soil calculation.
oven-dry basis
The sample mass after the specified drying step, before ignition, used as the denominator in this example.
interference
A process other than loss of organic matter that changes the recorded mass under a method.
